change.title: pr-38446-flat
change.description: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Storage-backed recovery codes get removed from the local DB, which does nothing
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` (RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56-62) now returns the user-storage credential first. When `allCodesUsed()` is true, this line still calls `removeStoredCredentialById(id)`. That goes to the local store (`UserCredentialManager.java:114-117`, `getStoreForUser`), and the local store never held this id, so the user-storage credential with no codes left stays in place. The storage still reports the user as configured. On the next login, `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` calls `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on an empty list (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:21) and throws. That happens if the user leaves before finishing the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action. For a federated credential, remove it through the storage, e.g. `credentialManager().disableCredentialType(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` (UserCredentialManager.java:173-188).

findings.title: Reference storage accepts any recovery code, as often as you like
findings.body: `isValid` accepts the input if it matches any stored code and never removes it. The local provider is stricter: it accepts only the next code and then removes it (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:106-112). With this storage, the login page asks for code #1 while any of the 12 codes works, and one code can be reused forever. `allCodesUsed()` never becomes true, so the new storage branch in the authenticator never runs. `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` logs in only once, so it can't catch reuse or wrong-code acceptance. Make the provider check only the next code and drop it after use. Then add a test that logs in twice and asserts the second login asks for code #2 and rejects code #1.

findings.title: Federated recovery-codes credential has a null id
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues` does not set an id, and `recoveryCodesModel.getId()` (set at line 195) is not copied over. The credential returned by `getCredentials` therefore has `id == null`. Account REST deletion looks up federated credentials with `credentialId.equals(c.getId())` (CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64), so this credential can't be selected or deleted. The authenticator's removal also gets a null id. Copy `myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()` onto the model.

findings.title: User storage receives plaintext codes and loses generatedAt and userLabel
findings.body: The storage gets only the raw codes as a JSON array in `challengeResponse`. The `generatedAt` and `userLabel` values from `credentialModel` (RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.java:110) are dropped, so each storage has to make up its own (the test storage uses `Time.currentTimeMillis()` and a null label). Every storage also has to hash and consume the codes itself, with no stated contract. Consider passing the hashed `credentialModel` data, or documenting what a storage must store and return from `getCredentials`. `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` depends on that returned model having hashed `secretData`.

contracts.action: Required action stores recovery codes via user storage first, local provider as fallback
contracts.equivalent_path: UserCredentialManager.updateCredential routes to the federation updater, then to local CredentialInputUpdater providers
contracts.before_after: Before: always went to the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential. After: user.credentialManager().updateCredential is tried first; the local provider only implements CredentialInputValidator, so non-federated users fall through to createCredential
contracts.visible_effect: Codes are stored in the external storage when it supports the type
contracts.failure_mode: If the storage's updateCredential returns false, codes are stored locally; JSON errors throw a RuntimeException

contracts.action: Authenticator and login bean read the recovery credential from federated storage first
contracts.equivalent_path: RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid reads the stored credential, consumes the code and updates the store
contracts.before_after: The local path consumes the code inside isValid; for the federated path, consuming is left to the storage, and on all-used the authenticator removes via the local store
contracts.visible_effect: Login page shows the next code number taken from the storage's model
contracts.failure_mode: When all codes are used, removeStoredCredentialById hits the local store and does nothing; the bean's .get() throws on an empty code list

summary: The PR lets recovery codes be stored in and read from user storage. Two problems with the storage-backed flow. First, when all codes are used, the authenticator still removes the credential from the local DB, which does nothing for a storage credential, so a credential with no codes left can remain and break the next login. Second, the reference test storage accepts any of the 12 codes, as many times as you like, and the new test only covers one login. Two smaller points: the federated credential has a null id, and the contract for what a user storage must hash, store and return is not stated.
